text:
Heisenberg's Uncertainty Principle can be understood by comparing it to trying to take a clear photograph of a fast-moving car at night. If you use a very fast shutter speed to freeze the car's position perfectly, the image becomes dark and blurry, making it impossible to tell how fast it was going. Conversely, if you use a slower shutter speed to capture the streak of light that shows its speed and direction, the car's exact location becomes smeared and uncertain. This mirrors the quantum reality that you cannot simultaneously know both the precise position and the precise momentum of a particle; the more precisely one is measured, the less precisely the other can be known.

The name of the planet humans live on is Earth.
